comments.author: @gubzs

Something people don't think about enough - these small test score improvements are HUGE leaps in model usability.
Think about it like this:
- An 86% correct model will fail roughly one in seven questions.
- A 95% correct model will fail roughly one in twenty.
- That 9% increase in test score represents a 200% increase in reliability.

comments.text: So I thought ok, lets get it to do a proof for an unsolved maths problem, for example the Riemann Hypothesis. The response was basically "As of my knowledge cutoff in Oct 2023...Since a proof or disproof has not been found yet, I cannot provide a proof.". So while I am in awe of the capabilities of these LLMs they still don't give us anything we don't already know. They are a tool, just like a calculator, that can speed up and\or automate the generation to finding results in an already known solution space. I certainly get why that is the case as LLMs trained on the reality we already know, but asking it to solve something new, just can't happen with this iteration of the technology. What has to change I wonder?

comments.author: @Sandro_g99
comments.text:
I think OpenAI is still holding back something much bigger than the model they just released. In my opinion, they are about a year or more ahead of the competition, as they have only recently reached the performance level of GPT-4. Knowing this, they are not at all concerned about releasing new models or features anytime soon. They launched an "Omni" model to surpass the competition. The competition managed to catch up with that model, and now they've launched a reasoning model. But none of this would scare someone working inside OpenAI on a daily basis, as they were already aware of these advances and knew this would happen.

Now, combining:

1. Agents (a base already launched in GPTs),


2. A multimodal model with audio, image, and video,


3. A reasoning model,


4. Long-term memory and planning,



All of this together in a single model, which I believe could be a GPT Next, a full Orion, or whatever name they choose to give it. That, indeed, would be something that could surprise someone like Ilya.

Okay - I'm quitting at 25:00. The USER doesn't want the entire chain of thought. There is no possible way to store it. Rather, the USER wants to query the model on its reasoning or to show a relevant chain. This could be 1-5% of the total process. This is actually typical of advanced Human Reasoning. We simply allow ourselves to go places and work quickly specifically to abort certain lines of reasoning and to discover new ones - perhaps to delete the problem entirely - something that the LLM doesn't have the luxury of doing - yet. So HUMANS DO NOT expend 100% of this mental energy but only 20% to judge the path - and it files 1% of that pending further discovery (i.e. in the World.)
Good Job Wes.
I PERSONALLY THINK that this process breaks the former process of cheating by digesting questions and answers in order to get to high scores. It shows just how difficult it is for a general LLM untrained in a very specific problem line, to successfully reason like a fully capable human. The entire geberative model is based on patterning. It's a huge accomplishment to develop a pattern recognition machine. However reasoning is not based on pattern recognition. LLM technology doesn't have what it takes to produce quality reasoning. That will have to work differently. You will never be able to "teach" and llm to actually think and reason. You can only feed it an endless array of partterns that it can then use to generate more patterns. If you feed it enough patterns it can mimic reasoning fairly well, but since it can't actually learn or reason, it can't deduce correct answers. It's merely generating patters that fit. 

I tested this thing all day yesterday and today. So, first 5 problems in, the bot is outright stupid. Rather than giving it the same 3 spent issues that don't really demonstrate reasoning at all, it should be given complex problems that you have to solve in real life. I don't see any advancement here whatsoever.
